content.title: Do You Know Who Is Controlling You from the Shadows?
content.subtitle: How your subconscious mind is being imprisoned under the guise of "freedom."
content.body:
Pause for a moment and ask yourself: were the decisions you made after waking up this morning truly yours? Research shows that an average smartphone user checks their phone 144 times a day and spends roughly 4 to 5 hours on screens. While you scroll, an ad or a reel flashes before your eyes, silently leaving an imprint on your subconscious mind.

Later in the day, while shopping or sharing an opinion with friends, that exact brand, lifestyle, or idea suddenly feels like the most logical choice! And you tell yourself, "Nobody influenced me—I chose this purely through my own independent thinking!"

In reality, by analyzing how many milliseconds you pause on a video or which websites you visit, algorithms build over 300 behavioral data points about your personality. Sitting thousands of miles away, psychologists and engineers use that data to manufacture your "personal choices."

The 'Illusion of Choice': A Truth Kept Hidden

In psychology and behavioral economics, this tactic is known as the Illusion of Choice. A silent rule of corporate psychology is: never force people with direct commands, because humans love to feel free. Instead, place two or three pre-selected options in front of them, so they believe the choice was entirely theirs.

When you walk into a supermarket and see dozens of different brands, a Cornell University study reveals that over 80% of them are owned by just a handful of multinational corporations. No matter which brand you pick, the profit goes into the exact same pocket.

When Slavery to Desires Is Called Modernity

The world keeps one vital truth hidden: when people push away the Creator’s guidance, thinking it restricts their freedom, they do not become free—they become slaves to far more dangerous, invisible forces.

Over a thousand years ago, Allah exposed this subtle slavery in the Noble Quran: "Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire?" (Surah Al-Furqan: 43). In Tafsir Ibn Kathir, it is explained that anyone whose sole standard for right and wrong is their personal whim actually worships their own desires.

Stop and reflect—will we spend our entire lives as puppets of algorithms, corporate ads, and our own desires? Or is it time we sought a way out of this invisible captivity? Remember, recognizing the cage is the first step toward freedom.

How to Break These Invisible Chains

Once you realize you are trapped in an invisible cage, half the battle is already won. Now is the time to open the door and step out. The true purpose of human life is not drifting along with algorithms or social currents, but using our intellect and conscience to submit to the will of our Lord. To reclaim this freedom, start with three simple steps today:

  • Pause and Question: Whenever you feel a strong urge to buy or follow something, pause for just 10 seconds and ask yourself, "Do I genuinely need this, or is an advertisement making me feel this way?"

  • Control Your Algorithm Diet: Unfollow unnecessary pages and consumerist content on social media that create artificial insecurity and restlessness within you.

  • Make the Creator’s Guidance Your Ultimate Standard: Companion Rib'i ibn Amir (may Allah be pleased with him) famously said, "Allah has sent us to deliver people from the servitude of creation to the servitude of the One Creator." Therefore, remember that true servitude to Allah is the only key to freedom from all invisible slavery.
